newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs trim gains, end up in rumor-driven mkt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs trim gains, end up in rumor-driven mkt.

text.p: After rising over two percent earlier, Brazil shares lost ground to end only modestly up amid the latest reports of corruption allegations involving a key government minister, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most traded stocks rose only 0.69 percent to 10,354 points after rising sharply most of the session.
Market volume was a heavy 793.08 million reais ($748.1 million).

Shares opened higher after investors digested the latest report by Folha de Sao Paulo daily on a purportedly taped legislator's conversation in which he allegedly said Communications Minister Sergio Motta gave him a television concession and cash in return for his vote on a re-election bill.

But late in the day the stock market was rattled by unconfirmed rumors that another local newspaper would publish fresh corruption allegations involving Motta and his handling of the upcoming Band B cellular sell-off, traders said.

Motta came under fire after Folha on Wednesday published a transcript of a purportedly taped conversation suggesting that he was involved in a vote-buying scheme in which five deputies allegedly received money to vote in favor of a bill allowing presidential re-election.
Motta on Wednesday strongly denied any wrongdoing, but the market responded to the Folha story falling 3.4 percent, the biggest drop in a single session this year.
Benchmark Telebras, which had risen over three percent earlier, closed up 0.23 percent at 130 reais Thursday.
Other blue-chips ended firmer. State oil firm Petrobras preferred rose 2.21 percent, ending at 231 reais.
Federal power utility Eletrobras preferred rose 1.19 percent to 512 reais.
Analysts said the market is likely to remain volatile Friday if speculation of new reports that could broaden the alleged scam continues.
